transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… thank you, doctor. I guess I’m here because my eating has been feeling a little out of control lately. It’s embarrassing to say, but after everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, and then somehow it turns into… a lot more. Like I’ll realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks were in the pantry, all in one sitting. I know that probably sounds bad.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate or control your weight?

I… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t do anything like that on purpose afterward. I usually just feel really awful and tell myself I’ll be “better” the next day, but I’m not making myself sick or taking things to undo it. Is that… is that what you mean?
Do these episodes of overeating cause you a lot of distress, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way?

I mean… I’m still functioning, I think. I’m keeping up with work and nobody there would probably know. But the mornings after, I feel really drained and just… ashamed, I guess. And I’ve started canceling or skipping things I usually like, like yoga or even time I set aside to be creative, because I just don’t want to face anyone. So… yes, it is affecting me, even if I’m trying to keep it contained.
Can you describe how quickly you eat during these episodes? Like, do you find yourself eating an unusually large amount of food in a short time, say within a couple of hours?

Um… yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it does happen pretty fast. I’ll be standing at the kitchen island, or sometimes scrolling through work emails, and I’m just eating without really… slowing down. Then I look down and the containers are empty, and I barely even remember tasting it. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual during these episodes, like you're rushing or not really chewing properly?

Yes… I think I do. I mean, not every single second, but during those times it’s like I’m just moving really quickly, standing at the kitchen island or looking through work emails, and I’m not really paying attention to chewing or tasting it. Then suddenly I look down and the containers are empty, and I feel like I barely registered what I was eating. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating, like it's happening on its own?

Yes… I think that’s probably the hardest part to admit. Once I start, especially if it’s been a tense night with my husband, it’s like the decision-making part of me just kind of… goes offline.

I’ll be thinking, “Patricia, stop, this is enough,” but my hand is still reaching for more. It doesn’t feel completely deliberate in that moment, even though I know that sounds like an excuse. It just feels really hard to interrupt once it’s started.
How often do these episodes happen? Like, would you say they occur at least once a week on average?

Um… yes, I think so. I’ve been trying not to overstate it, but for the last three months there’s been at least one night most weeks where it happens—usually after an argument or if I’m coming home late from a work event. And… some weeks it’s happened twice. So I guess, on average, yes, at least once a week.

There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors, which rules out bulimia nervosa (F50.9).
